svg.title: PRP — a protocol atlas
svg.desc: Technical architecture poster with SCIR, discovery, HS2 successor, TPA fast paths, relationships, group communication and versioned wire details.
svg.text: References → discovery → authenticated relationships → selected trajectories
Architecture, component protocols and selected binary layouts
A compact reference commits to canonical
material. Identity proof remains a separate
policy, Bloom views and exact lookup.
Flight labels are not wire-v4 opcodes.
RELATIVE TOPOLOGY • LOCAL SELECTORS • DISTINCT IDENTITY SCOPES
The client selects its trajectory. Each hop interprets a local context; an aggregator’s adjacency identity
does not reveal the identity carried inside the protected final channel.
Illustrative spacing; canonical text has no spaces.
Selectors are scoped per hop and realization.
Presentation is not a binary packet layout.
Membership and policy survive session changes.
Rekey, path replacement and retention have
Aggregation replicates delivery; it does not
An observed rate is not itself a reservation.
Exact layouts below belong to named working-draft profiles; widths are in octets.
Canonical inner payload follows. Generation binding and exact length are checked before use.
Successor session record: the complete protected packet
Experimental ChaCha20-Poly1305: tau = 16; nonce = derived 4-byte prefix + sequence. Nonce is not sent again.
The operation container inside AOP — one authenticated list, multiple scoped records
Fixed record header: 6 octets. Padding is not another record. Authenticate the AOP before dispatching operations.
HS2 / TPA: architectural direction; successor integration remains a separate scope.
AOP successor: sequence[8] + ciphertext + tag[tau]. Historical AOP: nonce[12] + ciphertext + tag[16].
SCIR, discovery and RRL are versioned formats; diagram widths are illustrative, not byte-proportional.
* Capacity negotiation: protocol-author clarification, 23 Oct 2026. Wire snapshot: 24 Oct 2026.
